description:
The Trade and Business Sector Scheme is an initiative launched by the Haryana Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (HSFDC) in Haryana, India. 

This scheme was introduced to promote entrepreneurship among the Scheduled Castes community in the state. 

The scheme was officially launched in the year 2008. 

The primary objective of the Trade and Business Sector Scheme is to provide financial assistance to Scheduled Castes individuals for starting their own businesses. 

The scheme aims to empower individuals by enabling them to become self-reliant and economically independent. 

The measurable targets of the scheme include the establishment of a minimum of 1,000 new businesses annually by Scheduled Castes individuals. 

The scheme also aims to provide skill development training to at least 2,000 individuals every year. 

The financial assistance under this scheme can go up to INR 10 lakh for each eligible beneficiary. 

The assistance is provided in the form of a loan at a subsidized interest rate of 6 percent per annum. 

The scheme also includes a provision for a subsidy of 30 percent on the project cost for setting up a new business. 

This subsidy is capped at a maximum of INR 1.5 lakh. 

Eligible beneficiaries can use this financial assistance for various business ventures including retail, manufacturing, and service sectors. 

To be eligible for the Trade and Business Sector Scheme, applicants must belong to the Scheduled Castes category. 

Applicants must be residents of Haryana and must be at least 18 years old. 

The maximum age limit for applicants is 55 years. 

The income criteria for eligibility state that the annual family income should not exceed INR 3 lakh. 

Educational qualifications are not strictly defined but having a basic understanding of business operations is beneficial. 

The application process for the Trade and Business Sector Scheme involves several steps. 

Interested individuals must first obtain the application form from the HSFDC office or download it from the official website. 

The completed application form must be submitted along with the required documents. 

Required documents include proof of Scheduled Caste certificate, identity proof, residence proof, and income certificate. 

Additionally, a detailed project report outlining the business plan is also necessary. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the HSFDC officials. 

The review process typically takes about 30 days. 

If the application is approved, the beneficiary will receive a sanction letter detailing the loan amount and subsidy. 

The disbursement of funds is usually completed within 15 days of receiving the sanction letter. 

The scheme also provides for a repayment period of 5 years for the loan amount. 

Beneficiaries are required to repay the loan in monthly installments. 

The implementing authority for the Trade and Business Sector Scheme is the Haryana Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation. 

The HSFDC is responsible for the overall administration and execution of the scheme. 

The corporation operates under the Department of Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes, Haryana. 

For any queries or assistance, beneficiaries can contact the HSFDC office located in Panchkula. 

The contact number for the HSFDC is 0172-2560910. 

The official website of HSFDC provides additional information and updates regarding the scheme. 

The scheme has been instrumental in promoting entrepreneurship among Scheduled Castes in Haryana. 

As of 2023, the scheme has facilitated the establishment of over 5,000 businesses across various sectors. 

The impact of the scheme has been significant in enhancing the economic status of the Scheduled Castes community. 

The scheme also contributes to the overall economic development of the state by creating job opportunities. 

Moreover, it encourages skill development and vocational training among the youth. 

The Trade and Business Sector Scheme is part of a broader initiative by the Government of Haryana to uplift marginalized communities. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 50 crore for the implementation of this scheme in the financial year 2023-2024. 

This budget allocation reflects the commitment of the state government towards the welfare of Scheduled Castes. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries who have successfully started their businesses. 

Many beneficiaries have reported an increase in their income levels and improved living standards. 

The scheme not only provides financial assistance but also offers mentorship and guidance to new entrepreneurs. 

Workshops and training sessions are conducted regularly to enhance the skills of beneficiaries. 

The Trade and Business Sector Scheme is a vital step towards achieving economic equality and social justice. 

It aligns with the national goal of promoting entrepreneurship and self-employment among marginalized communities. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's efforts in fostering an inclusive economy. 

In conclusion, the Trade and Business Sector Scheme by HSFDC is a comprehensive initiative aimed at empowering Scheduled Castes through entrepreneurship. 

With its structured financial assistance and support mechanisms, the scheme plays a crucial role in transforming lives and promoting economic development in Haryana. 

The ongoing success of the scheme underscores the importance of targeted welfare programs in achieving social equity. 

As the scheme continues to evolve, it is expected to reach even more beneficiaries in the coming years. 

The Trade and Business Sector Scheme exemplifies the potential of government initiatives in driving change and fostering self-reliance among disadvantaged communities.
